anomaly_def.Name: Buffer Cache and Latch Contention Anomaly + Storage I/O Throughput Anomaly + CPU Resource Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Buffer Cache and Latch Contention Anomaly: Sessions serialize on hot buffer pages, latches, or page-pin slots inside the buffer manager, stalling logical access to data despite available rows and indexes.
Storage I/O Throughput Anomaly: The physical volumes that hold data, temp, or log files are saturated for bandwidth, IOPS, or latency, throttling every read and write the database issues.
CPU Resource Anomaly: Database and background processes drive host CPU usage to sustained saturation, exhausting runnable-queue capacity and elongating scheduling latency.

When all three root causes strike together the system exhibits an extreme "triple choke" pattern: 1) Page-level latch waits and buffer-busy waits climb, often accompanied by high spin counts that burn CPU while real work stalls. 2) Physical read/write latency from the storage subsystem stretches far beyond normal, filling I/O queues and inflating data-file, log-write, and buffer-I/O wait events. 3) Overall CPU utilisation sits at or near 100 %, with elevated context switches and scheduler delays, yet throughput and commit rates fall, giving the appearance of a CPU bottleneck that does not improve even when additional cores are provisioned. Application sessions may pile up in a mixture of latch, buffer I/O, and CPU run-queue waits, making the dominant symptom oscillate from CPU saturation to I/O wait spikes, complicating troubleshooting efforts.

Causal chain: Storage saturation slows every buffer read, write, and checkpoint flush, forcing pages to stay pinned and latches to remain held longer; this inflates latch-contention windows and drives more sessions into spin-waits, which in turn consume extra CPU. The extra CPU burn crowds the scheduler, delaying the submission and completion of asynchronous I/Os, which further deepens the storage backlog. Meanwhile, prolonged dirty-page residency and frequent eviction caused by the constrained buffer pool amplify the need for physical I/O, feeding additional load into an already saturated storage layer. The feedback loop between slow I/O, extended latch holds, and runaway CPU consumption can cascade rapidly, crippling both transactional and analytical workloads until one or more resources are relieved.

entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with a general engine-level execution problem surfaced by the official error catalogue, but its precise trigger must be interpreted together with workload context and surrounding evidence.
entry.solution_guidance: Review the surrounding workload, official description, and engine state to determine whether the issue is rooted in SQL logic, resource pressure, configuration, or environmental instability.
